messages:
Maria Chen: Heads up — customer acmecorp is failing our OIDC SSO test: ID token rejected with aud mismatch and SCIM provisioning is creating duplicate users. stack trace below

Alex Kim: can you paste the raw error?

Maria Chen: sure — from our auth-proxy logs:
```
2026-03-20T14:22:11Z ERROR auth-proxy: token validation failed user=acmecorp-client err=invalid_audience expected=urn:redwood:api actual=https://accounts.acmecorp.com/oauth
```

Maria Chen: SCIM side shows 409 on user create, but payload seems identical; externalId differs only by trailing space sometimes. Also we saw KMS decrypt fail when trying to verify SCIM webhook signature: `decryption failed: context mismatch`

Ken Patel: hmm — two separate things but could be related to a recent config change. Did we rotate the KMS alias last week?

Jordan O'Neill: yes — there was a scheduled rekey for alias/rdw-scim-signer on 2026-03-18. CloudTrail shows a ReEncrypt call and new alias attached. No incidents reported though.

Alex Kim: the aud mismatch is likely our OIDC client config. The token's aud is the IDP's issuer URL — looks like the IDP is issuing tokens with their audience instead of our client_id. Did we change the SSO client_type or the audience mapping?

Maria Chen: We didn't touch the integration manually. Customer claims they updated their IdP config last week. But the SCIM duplicate issue points to normalization differences — maybe we changed how we canonicalize externalId after a deploy?

deploy-bot: deploy service/api@2026-03-18T03:00 UTC succeeded (hash: 1a2b3c). Trigger: infra/secret-rotate

Ken Patel: infra/secret-rotate? That could have swapped an env var. @Alex can you check SSO_AUDIENCE and CLIENT_ID in production?

Alex Kim: checking prod now — SSO_AUDIENCE is set to `urn:redwood:api` but last config change shows `SSO_AUDIENCE=https://accounts.acmecorp.com/oauth` in the deploy manifest on 2026-03-18 (maybe templating bug).

Maria Chen: so our service expected `urn:redwood:api` but the deployed value matched the token aud which caused rejection? seems backwards — the token had actual=https://accounts.acmecorp.com/oauth. Why would deploy manifest set audience to the idp issuer?

Ken Patel: I think our templating script mutated the value during secret-rotate, replacing placeholder `${IDP_ISSUER}` into SSO_AUDIENCE. That would make token validation compare urn:redwood:api vs https://... and fail. We'll revert to use CLIENT_ID for aud check and keep SSO_AUDIENCE for callback URLs only.

Jordan O'Neill: for SCIM `decryption failed: context mismatch` — looks like the signing key context we pass to KMS when decrypting the webhook signature doesn't match the context used to encrypt by the SCIM agent. After rekey, alias re-located and context changed (we add tenant id). If SCIM agent uses old context, decrypt fails. We saw CloudTrail: `Decrypt: KeyId arn:aws:kms:.../alias/rdw-scim-signer, EncryptionContext: {tenant: "acmecorp"}` but our consumer used `{tenant: "acme-corp"}` (dash vs no-dash).

Maria Chen: ahh — externalId trailing spaces + tenant id normalization mismatch explains duplicate users + decrypt. acmecorp's externalId mapping uses `ACME-001 ` (with trailing space) and our normalizer removed it for existing users but not for new provisioning flows.

Alex Kim: short-term plan: 1) revert SSO_AUDIENCE env var to CLIENT_ID-based validation on auth-proxy 2) patch SCIM consumer to accept normalized tenant values (strip spaces, casefold, replace dash) 3) re-enqueue failed SCIM jobs with dedupe check on normalized externalId 4) rotate KMS alias mapping to ensure consistent EncryptionContext semantics and document it

Ken Patel: I'll open a quick PR to add normalization helpers and a canary toggle. keeping it behind feature flag so we can roll forward slowly.

Maria Chen: can someone run a sanity check curl against introspection endpoint? here's what I ran locally that failed:
```
curl -X POST https://auth.redwood.example/introspect -d 'token=eyJhbGci..'  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded'
# response: {"active":false, "error":"invalid_audience"}
```

Alex Kim: after reverting SSO_AUDIENCE to use CLIENT_ID on auth-proxy (patched in staging), introspection returns active:true. I pushed the config rollback to prod in a hotfix deploy.

deploy-bot: hotfix deploy auth-proxy@2026-03-20T15:05 UTC succeeded (hash: 4f5e6d)

Jordan O'Neill: requeued 18 failed SCIM jobs for acmecorp with normalization applied. 12 succeeded, 6 still 409 — those had exact externalId collision even after trimming. I'm running a reconcile job to merge duplicates safe-mode.

Maria Chen: thanks team. follow-ups: Ken please PR the normalization and add unit tests for externalId -> normalized_external_id. Ken please also add a migration script to merge duplicate users when normalized id matches. Jordan please document KMS encryption context conventions in runbook (tenant canonicalization rules). Alex please add a monitoring alert if SSO_AUDIENCE and CLIENT_ID diverge in prod config (config drift).

Ken Patel: on it, will target PR today. :+1:

Alex Kim: created alert draft in pagerduty config, pinging infra to review.

security-bot: note: filed vuln ticket VULN-2026-114 (low) for potential config templating substitution bug affecting SSO config. Assigned to Ken Patel.

Maria Chen: closing loop — customer confirmed SSO test now passes and provisioning backfill cleared. I'll follow up with a short incident blameless postmortem tomorrow. :wave:
